Going to (6,1,4) would force the line onto number 7 before its turn. So the line goes to (4,1,2).

Number 7 is next and right here, so the line takes it.

Going to (4,2,7) would strand number 8: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes to (6,1,6).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,1,6).
Going to (1,2,6) leaves no safe move afterwards; going to (2,4,7), the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,2,6). So the line goes to (2,1,6).

Going to (1,4,6) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (1,2,4).

Going to (1,2,2) would strand number 12: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going to (1,4,4) would strand number 12: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes to (2,1,4).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,1,2).
Going to (2,2,1) would leave both cell (1,2,2) and cell (4,2,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes to (1,2,2).
The line must go to (2,2,1): to (1,4,2) is number 19, which comes later.
Cell (4,2,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,4,1).
Going to (2,4,1), the next 11 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,7,4). So the line goes to (4,6,1).
Number 14 is only reachable this way.
Going to (4,7,4) would leave number 15 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (6,7,2).
Going to (7,6,2) would turn number 15 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes to (6,6,1).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (7,6,2).

Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (6,7,6).
Going to (2,7,6) would wall in number 21, the last number. So the line goes to (1,6,4).
Going to (1,4,4) would cut off a group of 5 cells; going to (1,6,6) would leave number 18 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (1,6,2).
Going to (2,6,1) would turn number 18 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes to (2,7,2).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,6,1).
Cell (2,4,7) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,6,7).
Cell (1,6,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,7,6).
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
